item.intervention_or_exposure: MDMA; study doses and regimens varied
item.outcome_or_entity: Self-reported sociability-related outcomes, including feeling loving, talkative, friendly, sociable, and extraverted
item.timepoint_or_window: Acute experimental drug sessions; exact assessment windows varied or were not reported

effect_estimate.adjustment_status: Accounted for dependencies among effect sizes nested within studies

heterogeneity.authors_interpretation: The Q-test indicated heterogeneity in the effect sizes.

analysis_context.dependency_handling: Modeled effect-size variance, between-outcome-within-study variance, and between-study variance.

interpretation.favors: MDMA over placebo for self-reported sociability-related outcomes

interpretation.authors_interpretation: The authors characterize the effect as moderate to large and caution that significant heterogeneity warrants careful interpretation.

evidence_locators.supporting_text: the average effect of MDMA on sociability is moderate to large (d = 0.86; 95% CI [0.68, 1.04]
A Q-test was significant (χ 2 (53) = 173.1, p = 1.2 x 10 -14 ), indicating heterogeneity

limitations: The included studies varied in design and operationalization of subjective outcomes.
The analysis included placebo comparisons only, not active-control comparisons.
Participants were largely sampled from Western, educated, industrialized cultures, and no clinical samples were included.
Many studies assessed sociability as a secondary outcome, and participants were typically tested alone.
